risks.description: A release requested without a valid signed credential (unauthenticated / non-supervisor stand-in) is not refused, or is refused but still advances/claims the operation, violating 'a non-supervisor is refused and no release occurs'.
risks.basis: AC 'a non-supervisor is refused and no release occurs'; /actions/signed and /email/action are the only release entry points, guarded by signature verification in handle_signed_action_callback (action_callback.py:137-193).

risks.description: A refused release leaves no durable record. The signed-action intake (/actions/signed, /email/action) returns a 401/400 refusal but — unlike the Slack operation-approval route — records NO security_events/audit_events row, so 'every refusal is recorded in the audit log' fails on that route.
risks.basis: AC 'every refusal is recorded in the audit log'; add_security_event is called on the Slack operation route (action_callback.py:434-438,477-481) but handle_signed_action_callback (137-193) emits no such record on rejection.

risks.description: The role-gated release path is not reachable on the deployed server: /slack/actions returns 404 unless a Slack signing secret is configured, and run_action_callback_server hardwires operation_router=None, so no supervisor can release at all (AC-1 unmet by unreachability rather than by a role check).
risks.basis: run_action_callback_server.py:133 sets operation_router=None; action_callback.py:260-276 returns 404 for /slack/actions when slack_signing_secret is None.

risks.description: Cross-tenant release is possible: WorkflowStore.release_operation_commit performs an unqualified reservation release ('Tenant A could release tenant B's reservation'), so a supervisor of one tenant may release another tenant's operation.
risks.basis: AC 'a supervisor of one tenant cannot release another tenant's operation'; workflow.py:906-910 docstring states the release is not tenant-qualified.

risks.description: Supervisor role is undefined in the persisted model — no roles/role column exists in the canonical schema — so 'supervisor vs non-supervisor' cannot be evaluated authoritatively and may be inferred from a spoofable request field.
risks.basis: Grep of schema.py and migrations/phase2_tenant_first.py finds no role/supervisor table or column; acceptance criteria require a supervisor/non-supervisor distinction.

risks.description: Replaying an already-used release approval releases twice (no idempotency), producing a duplicate external effect.
risks.basis: claim_operation_action guards single-use (action_callback.py:535-552); a role-gated release must preserve that guard — unverifiable without a valid token.

scenarios.title: Canonical schema materializes the audit substrate refusals depend on
scenarios.purpose: Confirm the database the product builds actually contains security_events and audit_events, the only tables where a refused release can be durably recorded. If either is absent, the 'every refusal is recorded' criterion is impossible regardless of handler logic.
scenarios.rationale: AC-4 (every refusal recorded) is only meaningful if a durable audit table exists in the canonical schema the release path writes to.
scenarios.generating_risk: A refused release has nowhere to be recorded because the audit substrate is missing from the schema.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-AUTHZ-2 AC 'every refusal is recorded in the audit log'

actions.name: canonical schema table list
actions.command: .venv/bin/python -c "import sqlite3,tempfile,os,sys; sys.path.insert(0,'src'); from freight_recon.schema import create_canonical_schema; p=os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(),'probe.sqlite3'); c=sqlite3.connect(p); create_canonical_schema(c); print(sorted(r[0] for r in c.execute(\"select name from sqlite_master where type='table'\")))"

scenarios.isolation_note: Builds a throwaway schema in a fresh tempdir; touches no shared DB or port, so it cannot contaminate any other scenario.

scenarios.title: Unauthenticated release request is refused and releases nothing
scenarios.purpose: A release POST carrying no signed credential (the stand-in for a caller with no supervisor authority) must be refused at the front door and must not start or claim any operation.
scenarios.rationale: Directly probes 'a non-supervisor is refused and no release occurs' for the strongest non-supervisor: a caller presenting no authority at all.
scenarios.generating_risk: An operation is released for a caller who presented no valid authority.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-AUTHZ-2 AC 'a non-supervisor is refused and no release occurs'

persisted_state_checks.name: system actor never released an operation
persisted_state_checks.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT count(*) FROM security_events WHERE event_type='slack_operation_started' AND actor='system'"

scenarios.isolation_note: A refused request creates at most an append-only system-actor row; the oracle counts started-operations by the system actor (an invariant zero), so appended refusal rows cannot make another scenario pass or fail.

scenarios.title: Forged release token is rejected and the operation is never started
scenarios.purpose: A release request bearing an unverifiable (forged) signed token must be rejected as unverifiable and must not advance any operation to a started/running state.
scenarios.rationale: Exercises the refusal path for a caller who fakes authority; pairs the HTTP refusal with a persisted-state oracle that no release occurred, as AC-2 requires.
scenarios.generating_risk: A forged credential is accepted and the operation is released.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-AUTHZ-2 AC 'a non-supervisor is refused and no release occurs'

persisted_state_checks.name: no system-actor operation start after forged token
persisted_state_checks.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT count(*) FROM security_events WHERE event_type='slack_operation_started' AND actor='system'"

scenarios.isolation_note: Refused request is non-mutating except for possible append-only audit rows; the oracle is an invariant-zero count unaffected by appends.

scenarios.title: Email release link with no token fails closed
scenarios.purpose: The email-channel release action link must refuse an unauthenticated release identically to the JSON route, so authorization cannot be bypassed by switching channels.
scenarios.rationale: AC-2 must hold on every release entry point; the GET /email/action link is a distinct code path (query-token, GET) from the POST JSON route and could regress independently.
scenarios.generating_risk: The email release link accepts an unauthenticated release that the JSON route would refuse.
scenarios.requirement_reference: U-AUTHZ-2 AC 'a non-supervisor is refused and no release occurs'

persisted_state_checks.name: system actor never released via email link
persisted_state_checks.command: sqlite3 data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3 "SELECT count(*) FROM security_events WHERE event_type='slack_operation_started' AND actor='system'"

scenarios.isolation_note: Read-only refusal path; no removable state created.

assumptions: The local app at 127.0.0.1:8001 is the run_action_callback_server callback service (service_refs: callback) bound to the driver_probe workspace DB at data/active_workspace/driver_probe/workflow.sqlite3.
Release of an operation is realized through the signed-action / operation-approval intake in action_callback.py; there is no separate unsigned 'release' HTTP endpoint.
The server is running when request-based scenarios execute; if it is not, those scenarios will fail on connection rather than on product behavior.
'security_events' is the recording table for authorization refusals at the transport boundary and 'audit_events' for run-scoped decisions, per phase2_tenant_first.py.
A refused release never carries actor='system' into a 'slack_operation_started' event, making that count an invariant zero usable as a 'no release occurred' oracle.
unresolved_questions: What is the concrete release contract the builder added? The task names an 'operator console' but the console in-repo (operator_console.py) is a static HTML page; the only live release path requires a Slack- or delivery-signed token. No release endpoint that takes a supervisor identity in a driveable form is visible.

How is 'supervisor' represented and checked? The canonical schema (schema.py, phase2_tenant_first.py) has no roles table or role column, and code today authorizes by Slack user/channel allowlist. Without a persisted role model, the supervisor/non-supervisor distinction (AC-1, AC-2) cannot be authoritatively evaluated.

AC-1 (a supervisor CAN release) is not verifiable with the approved commands: none of them can mint a valid signed release token, and run_action_callback_server hardwires operation_router=None so the approval path is inert/unreachable. A signed-token fixture or a supervisor-authenticated release endpoint is needed to exercise the happy path.

AC-3 (cross-tenant supervisor cannot release another tenant's operation) is not exercisable: it requires two provisioned tenants each with a valid supervisor release token. Note workflow.py:906 documents that release_operation_commit is NOT tenant-qualified — this should be reviewed as a likely cross-tenant defect.

Does a refused release on the /actions/signed and /email/action routes actually write to security_events/audit_events? Those handlers (handle_signed_action_callback) return 401/400 but appear NOT to record, unlike the Slack operation-approval route — a probable AC-4 gap that needs a token-minting fixture to confirm end to end.

Is a before/after audit-log delta observable? With single approved sqlite commands and no ability to snapshot-then-compare, 'a NEW refusal row was written by THIS request' cannot be asserted precisely; only invariant properties (e.g. system actor never starts an operation) are robust.
